## Mombacho Volcano: cloud forest above Granada

Mombacho lies near [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), on the western shore of [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/). Beyond the city streets, the road climbs toward a volcano covered in dense greenery. Mombacho reaches an altitude of 1,345 m, but reaching the summit itself is not the main reason to visit. Travelers come for the humid cloud forest, walking trails and views across the lake and Granada Islets.

The air along the forest trails is often damp, and clouds may obscure distant panoramas on the upper slopes. That makes Mombacho interesting even on an overcast day: you can examine ferns, orchids, mosses and the changes in vegetation within a relatively small area. If your priority is photographing the lake from above, keeping the visiting time somewhat flexible around the weather can help.

## What to see on Mombacho

### Cloud forest and volcanic slopes

The protected area covers the volcano's cloud forest. Large ferns, epiphytes, orchids and bromeliads grow beside the trails, and the forest can become shrouded in mist. Birds and howler monkeys inhabit the area. Wildlife encounters depend on timing, weather and luck: visiting the reserve does not guarantee a safari.

Mombacho's volcanic history can be seen in the shape of its slopes and crater areas. A self-guided walk along a nature trail, a guided outing on a more demanding route and a canopy adventure are different activities; they should not be treated as interchangeable when choosing a tour.

### Viewpoints over the lake

In clear weather, the trails open up views of [Las Isletas, the Granada Islets](/nicaragua/place/granada-islets/) and the broad expanse of Cocibolca, another name for Lake Nicaragua. The contrast is striking: thick forest underfoot, water and small green islands far below.

Protecting your camera against moisture is helpful. If clouds hide the views, the experience of the forest itself remains worthwhile, rather than waiting for one particular panorama.

## Trails or canopy: which experience should you choose?

The natural reserve has trails of varying difficulty. For example, the reserve's operator describes the Tigrillo Trail as a moderate walk through cloud forest and viewpoints. Other sections may require an accompanying guide and greater physical fitness. Check which trails are currently open, access rules and walking times when planning: these depend on the selected route and local conditions.

Canopy activities involve crossing specially equipped cable sections above the forest. It is an active adventure with safety instruction and participant requirements, rather than a walking excursion to the crater. Travelers who want to study plants and watch birds may prefer the trails. Those who enjoy movement and views among the treetops may find canopy more appealing.

We offer a standalone [“Granada Islets and Mombacho Canopy” excursion](/nicaragua/granada-islets/granada-islets-mombacho-canopy/). It begins with a boat trip among the lake islets, followed by a half-day canopy program on Mombacho. This is a specific combination, not a promise to cover all of the reserve's hiking trails.

## Planning a visit from Granada

Granada makes a convenient base for Mombacho. The lower part of the reserve can be reached by road; onward travel on steep stretches follows local vehicle-access rules. Do not assume an ordinary passenger car can reach every upper trail.

Bring shoes with grippy soles, water, light rain protection and clothing comfortable for walking on damp ground. It may be hot below and cooler and wetter higher up. Allow separate time for the drive, reserve admission, the activity itself and the return.

A practical way to explore the area is to devote some time to [historic Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), visit the [lake islets](/nicaragua/place/granada-islets/) and then head to Mombacho. Choose your priority: boat, forest trail or canopy. On day four of our [10-day “Best of Nicaragua” itinerary](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/), travelers visit the Granada Islets and take a Mombacho canopy adventure; the other days include León, Masaya, Ometepe and the Pacific coast.

## Mombacho and Masaya Volcano: what's the difference?

[Masaya Volcano National Park](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) is chiefly associated with volcanic craters and volcanic terrain. Mombacho provides another side of volcanic nature: cloud forest, walks amid tropical vegetation and lake views. Both are near Granada, but the experiences and their requirements differ.

For families with children or travelers unused to long hikes, choose a particular accessible route in advance rather than relying only on the word “volcano.” A challenging trail, an easy walk and canopy activities require different preparation.

## Frequently asked questions about Mombacho Volcano

### Can we visit Mombacho without a long ascent?

Yes. A visit to the reserve does not necessarily mean hiking all the way from the foot of the mountain. Access to upper areas is arranged using permitted transport, followed by a suitable trail or activity. Exact arrangements depend on local conditions.

### Which is more interesting: Mombacho or the Granada Islets?

Mombacho is known for cloud forest and scenic trails. The [Granada Islets](/nicaragua/place/granada-islets/) are better for a relaxed boat trip across the lake. You can combine them in one day if the itinerary and timing allow.

### Can we see wildlife during a walk?

Birds and other animals inhabit the forest, but particular species cannot be guaranteed. A quiet pace and attentive observation matter more than covering as many kilometers as possible.

### Is a walking trail included in the Ada Tours excursion?

Our [Granada Islets program](/nicaragua/granada-islets/granada-islets-mombacho-canopy/) includes a half-day canopy adventure. A separate hike and its arrangements would need to be agreed independently.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with [Mombacho Volcano](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/) as a main stop. ## Day four: Granada Islets and canopy adventure

The morning includes a **private boat trip** around the [Granada Islets, Las Isletas](/nicaragua/place/granada-islets/). These small, green islands lie in [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/), with the Mombacho massif visible from the water. Birds may be seen on the lake, while encounters with wild animals depend on nature and cannot be guaranteed.

A **half-day canopy program on Mombacho** follows. The humid mountain forest, ferns and mist-covered sections differ markedly from Granada's warmer city streets. More details about the combined excursion appear on the [“Granada Islets and Mombacho Canopy” page](/nicaragua/granada-islets/granada-islets-mombacho-canopy/).

Breakfast and lunch are scheduled for day four, along with guiding, transport and admission tickets according to the itinerary. The group spends the night in Granada. The price of the canopy activity within this tour is not automatically added as a separate charge to the overall tour price.

However, **the exact canopy course and participant requirements must be confirmed before booking**. The word “canopy” does not mean the traveler will ascend the summit or undertake a difficult mountain trek.

## Canopy, forest walking and climbing: how they differ

Mombacho offers several types of nature experience, each with its own access arrangements.

| Format | Main feature |
|---|---|
| Canopy | Suspended lines among the trees |
| Walking | Observing mountain nature |
| Climbing | A separate physical challenge |
| Scenic viewpoints | Lake and surrounding Granada area |

**The current Ada Tours itinerary explicitly includes a half-day canopy experience**, rather than a sporting ascent. If hiking the volcano's slopes is your priority, choose an excursion where trails are included separately, with confirmed duration, access rules and physical demands.

The cloud forest is known for its vegetation and shifting visibility. Moisture settles on leaves high on the slopes, while views of the lake appear and disappear through mist. The forest itself is worth visiting; a permanent panorama or sighting of a specific animal cannot be promised.

Read more about the natural attraction on the [Mombacho page](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/), or explore other active journeys among [Nicaragua adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/nicaragua/).

## How Mombacho combines with Granada and Masaya

**Granada** is a convenient base for day four: both the lake islets and the volcanic massif lie nearby. The previous day, day three, includes [Granada's](/nicaragua/place/granada/) historic center, [Masaya Volcano National Park](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) and Masaya's craft market.

They offer different experiences. Masaya is associated with the volcano's national park and volcanic geography, whereas Mombacho is about humid forest and canopy adventure. They should not be considered the same excursion merely because both involve volcanoes. Moreover, **access to Masaya's crater and the particular canopy route must be confirmed when arranging the journey**.

If you have limited time in Nicaragua, Granada, the islets and Mombacho bring together city, lake and mountain forest in one area. But the current ten-day itinerary has a defined sequence of days, best understood by reading the [full tour itinerary](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/).

## Who this journey suits and what to pack

Mombacho day appeals to those who enjoy **activities surrounded by nature**, within a varied sightseeing trip. The tour is not all about exertion: the volcano days are followed by an island stage and free time on the coast. The format is specified **for groups of 2 or more people**, with English-speaking guided excursions according to the itinerary.

Bring closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles, light rain protection and clothing suitable for damp air. Even if Granada is sunny, cloud forest weather may feel different. Age and physical restrictions for the specific canopy course should be checked separately; the published description does not specify universal admission criteria.

Mombacho is only one stop in a bigger journey. On day five, the route passes through [San Jorge](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/) to [Ometepe](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/), then continues to the Pacific coast. If you are more interested in the island or the spring pools, compare those days rather than choosing the entire tour only for canopy.

## Questions about tours visiting Mombacho

### Is Mombacho included on the main itinerary?

Yes. On the [ten-day Nicaragua tour](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/), the volcano is a main destination. Canopy activities are scheduled on day four with the boat trip around Las Isletas.

### Is there a climb to the volcano's summit?

The published itinerary specifies a half-day **canopy adventure**, not a sporting ascent. These are not interchangeable activities.

### Can we see Mombacho and the Granada Islets in one day?

Yes. That is exactly how day four is arranged: first a private boat trip among the islets, then an introduction to Mombacho's cloud forest and canopy.

### Which part of the journey focuses on nature?

The nature itinerary includes Lake Nicaragua, Mombacho, the Masaya volcanic region and Ometepe Island. Free days in San Juan del Sur follow these stages. All are described in the [“Best of Nicaragua” itinerary](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/).

### Is canopy suitable for every traveler?

Participation depends on the specific course and operator's rules. Confirm the route, physical requirements and restrictions before booking. Ages, heights and weights are not stated in the published itinerary.

## Ojo de Agua: a natural spring on Ometepe Island

Ojo de Agua is a place to relax beside clear freshwater on [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/) in Nicaragua. Pools fed by a natural underground spring are set among tropical trees. Travelers come to swim or simply rest beside the water after a journey, an island walk or a volcanic excursion.

What distinguishes Ojo de Agua from Ometepe's lakeside beaches is that spring water flows into developed pools. A relaxation area surrounds them, but entry arrangements, swimming rules and available services should be checked before a visit. This is a distinct stop on an island journey, not another volcano or lake.

## Where the spring is and how to reach it

Ojo de Agua is in the municipality of Altagracia, in the Santo Domingo area of Ometepe. The island itself lies in [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/), among the lake's shores and two volcanoes, Concepción and Maderas. To reach it from the mainland, visitors generally first travel to the [San Jorge ferry terminal](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/), then continue by road after landing on the island.

Because the journey includes a lake crossing, the time available at Ojo de Agua depends on the ferry schedule and the order of other stops. On a day trip, the last return service is particularly important. If you have several days on the island, the spring makes a convenient stop between more active outings without rushing from one sight to the next.

## What Ojo de Agua is like

### Freshwater pools shaded by trees

Natural spring water flows into purpose-built pools, while the trees provide shade. Visitors can spend time both in the water and beside it. Unlike the open shore of a large lake, the site is arranged around a specific spring with designated swimming areas.

Water clarity, depth in different areas, visitor numbers and comfort depend on actual conditions. If visiting with children, check the depth of the chosen pool and supervision rules rather than assuming every area is shallow.

### Relaxing after the road and volcano trails

Ometepe is known for Concepción and Maderas volcanoes, walking trails and rural landscapes. Ojo de Agua offers something different: a chance to pause by the water without a long hike. This is especially welcome after a drive or walk, when another demanding climb is not needed.

The island is rewarding even without swimming: natural shores, volcano views and cultural heritage appear throughout an [Ometepe journey](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/). The spring is one stop, not a substitute for exploring the island.

## How much time to allow and what to bring

Leave time not only for the pool but also for changing clothes, resting and traveling back. If you have just one day on the island, first check the ferry arrival, actual travel time to the spring and the return crossing. A precise visit duration cannot be set without the timetable and details of the excursion.

Bring swimwear, a towel, footwear suitable for wet surfaces and dry clothes. Protect valuables from water, and check the pool entrance and posted rules before swimming. Natural spring water alone is not proof of medicinal effects: visit for relaxation and the surroundings.

## Ojo de Agua on an Ada Tours itinerary

On our [“Best of Nicaragua: Volcanoes, Ometepe and the Pacific” tour](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/), Ojo de Agua is visited on day five. The route includes a transfer to San Jorge, a ferry to Ometepe and a stop at the natural spring pools. The following day involves returning to the mainland and continuing to San Juan del Sur.

There is also a standalone [“Ometepe and Ojo de Agua with Ferry Crossing” excursion](/nicaragua/ometepe-island/ometepe-ojo-de-agua-ferry/). It describes the island journey and spring visit; swimming time, the ferry schedule and extra conditions are agreed when organizing the trip. Including Ojo de Agua does not mean that every possible water activity or facility at the site is covered by the price.

If you are primarily choosing a journey for nature, explore [nature-themed destinations and trips](/interests/nature/). Ojo de Agua is a place to rest beside water, not a location where specialist observation of rare species is necessarily organized.

## Frequently asked questions about Ojo de Agua

### Is Ojo de Agua on the mainland or an island?

On [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/) in Lake Nicaragua. From the mainland, allow for a ferry crossing and onward road travel.

### Are the pools filled with seawater or freshwater?

Freshwater. They are fed by a natural underground spring; Ometepe itself sits in a large freshwater lake.

### Can we stop here without swimming?

Yes. Visitors can enjoy the natural surroundings and relax beside the water. Entry charges and site rules apply whether or not you swim, so check the terms beforehand.

### Can Ojo de Agua be included in a day trip?

Yes, if the ferry and road schedule allow it. The last return sailing is especially important on an independent visit; the [Ada Tours excursion](/nicaragua/ometepe-island/ometepe-ojo-de-agua-ferry/) includes the crossing, with the actual timetable agreed when arranging the trip.

## Day five: crossing the lake and stopping at the spring

The day starts with a road transfer to [San Jorge port](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/) for a **ferry crossing of Lake Nicaragua** to [Ometepe Island](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/). After arrival, the group visits Ojo de Agua, a complex of natural pools supplied by an underground spring. Breakfast is also scheduled for this day.

The route is described in the separate [“Ometepe and Ojo de Agua with Ferry Crossing” excursion](/nicaragua/ometepe-island/ometepe-ojo-de-agua-ferry/). It clarifies the order: mainland port and lake first, then the island and natural spring. **The ferry is an essential part of the transport arrangements.**

After the spring, the group spends the night on Ometepe. Villa Colonial and Villa Paraiso are named as accommodation options in the tour documents; the final hotel and overnight arrangements are confirmed before booking. On day six, travelers return by ferry to San Jorge and continue to the Pacific coast.

## What Ojo de Agua is like

[Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/) lies among Ometepe's dense vegetation. Natural underground spring water feeds the developed pools. Visitors come to unwind beside the water and change pace after traveling.

The site differs from the open beaches of [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/). Here, you can spend time at pools under trees, while the lake shore has open water, wind and long stretches of coastline. **The published tour explicitly confirms the visit**, but does not list a specific swimming period, personal amenities or extra site services as guaranteed package inclusions.

| Place | Why visit |
|---|---|
| [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/) | Rest beside spring water |
| [Ometepe](/nicaragua/place/ometepe-island/) | Volcanoes and island nature |
| [Mombacho](/nicaragua/place/mombacho-volcano/) | Cloud forest and canopy |
| [San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/) | Days on the Pacific coast |

This makes it easier to match a trip to your priorities: the spring is a quiet stop, whereas an active volcano day or several days by the sea involve different activities.

## Swimming: what is actually confirmed?

The Ometepe–Ojo de Agua excursion describes the pools as a place to relax in clear water. **Visiting time and swimming conditions are agreed when arranging the journey.** A stop on the itinerary is not an unconditional promise that travelers can swim in all weather, regardless of opening hours or the site's condition.

If you plan to enter the water, bring swimwear, a towel and dry clothes. For the ferry day, a small bag protecting belongings from splashes and rain is helpful. These are personal packing suggestions: the published program does not confirm that rental gear, lockers, on-site food or other services are included.

The ten-day tour price includes admission to attractions listed in the program, transport and English-speaking guided excursions according to the itinerary. **Separate optional activities and personal expenses** are not included. The terms for booking a standalone Ometepe excursion are set separately and must not be confused with the published tour package.

## Planning an island day with a ferry

Day five involves two kinds of transport: the road to San Jorge and the ferry to the island. The departure and the possibility of visiting Ojo de Agua afterward depend on the actual timetable and weather. Even if the spring itself takes relatively little time, **the day cannot be treated as a simple out-and-back trip from Granada**: the published route includes an overnight stay on Ometepe.

On a short trip, distinguish transfers from excursions: listing Ometepe does not automatically mean an ascent of Concepción or Maderas, visits to every beach or all the island's archaeological sites.

On the next day, the [ten-day route](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/) continues to San Juan del Sur, where free days are scheduled. If detailed exploration of Ometepe is your primary goal, consider the number of nights on the island rather than simply counting named sights.

## Why Ojo de Agua works well on a longer journey

After city walks and a more active canopy day on Mombacho, a stop beside the water offers a change of pace. Before Ometepe, the tour includes sightseeing in Granada, Masaya Volcano and a boat trip around the islets. After Ojo de Agua comes the journey toward the ocean and several days of relaxation.

**The order matters when choosing this tour.** Ojo de Agua belongs to a program combining history, nature and a beach section. It suits travelers who enjoy alternating activities rather than climbing or taking part in sports every day.

The full itinerary, including accommodation and transport arrangements, is published on the [“Best of Nicaragua” tour page](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/). For comparison, explore [Nicaragua tours](/nicaragua/tour/) and [nature-themed journeys in the country](/interests/wildlife/tours/nicaragua/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Ojo de Agua

### Is Ojo de Agua included in the tour price or optional?

**The visit is on the main itinerary** of the current ten-day program. Admission tickets according to the route are specified. Swimming and any additional services require confirmation of the conditions at the stop.

### Which day of the tour includes the spring?

**Day five.** Travelers first drive to San Jorge port, then take the ferry to Ometepe and visit Ojo de Agua.

### Do we have to climb a volcano to reach Ojo de Agua?

No. The tour includes a stop at the natural pools, not an ascent of Concepción or Maderas. Any climbing must be listed and confirmed separately.

### Can we visit Ojo de Agua and return to Granada on the same day?

The current itinerary is arranged differently: the spring visit is followed by **an overnight stay on Ometepe**, and the ferry return takes place the next day. Different private transport arrangements cannot be inferred from this tour's published terms.

### Is there time for swimming?

The pool visit is included, but **the precise length of the stop and swimming arrangements** are agreed when organizing the journey. No fixed swimming duration is specified in the public itinerary.

The [“Ometepe and Ojo de Agua with Ferry” excursion page](/nicaragua/ometepe-island/ometepe-ojo-de-agua-ferry/) describes the island portion. The [ten-day tour](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/) shows how it connects to Granada and the Pacific coast.

## Ometepe Island: two volcanoes in the middle of Lake Nicaragua

**Ometepe** sits in Lake Cocibolca, also known as [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/). Its outline is formed by two volcanic massifs joined by a lower isthmus. Concepción rises in the northwest and Maderas in the southeast. From the shore, travelers see broad views of the water and volcanic slopes, while villages, farmland and forest alternate across the island.

The island was recognized as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2010. It appeals both to people wanting mountain trails and to travelers who prefer nature walks without major elevation gain. The [Nicaragua destinations catalog](/nicaragua/place/) provides a broader overview; here the focus is on exploring the island itself.

## Concepción or Maderas: how the volcanoes differ

Concepción is a tall, active volcano with a distinct cone; UNESCO gives its height as **1,610 m**. Maderas rises to **1,394 m** and is known for the humid forests of its higher slopes. The summit hikes differ in trail surfaces, weather and required preparation.

| Volcano | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| Concepción | Exposed slopes and steep elevation gain |
| Maderas | Humid forest and more slippery trails |

A complete ascent requires physical fitness, suitable footwear and a route chosen according to local regulations and current volcanic conditions. Mist can obscure the views from Maderas, while heavy rain can make dirt paths much more difficult. **The presence of these volcanoes in the island description does not mean that an ascent is included in every Ometepe tour.**

Choose a hiking activity separately from a general island tour. [Nicaragua adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/nicaragua/) help compare the actual level of activity, not just itinerary titles.

## What to see on Ometepe without climbing

You can experience the island through lakeside walks, volcano views and natural springs. [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/) is known for its pools fed by an underground spring. It is suitable for a quieter day without a long mountain hike.

Ometepe has the settlements of Moyogalpa and Altagracia, as well as forest and rural landscapes. Ancient petroglyphs and archaeological finds are an important part of the island's heritage. UNESCO highlights the value of pre-Hispanic sites around Maderas. Any visit to a particular archaeological site should be confirmed in the actual itinerary rather than confused with a general sightseeing stop.

Birds and other tropical animals inhabit the natural areas, but sightings cannot be guaranteed at a particular time. If nature is the main reason for your journey, compare [Nicaragua wildlife and nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/nicaragua/) and choose a program with adequate observation time.

## Reaching the island and planning the ferry

Ometepe is separated from the mainland by the lake. One of the principal routes goes through [San Jorge port](/nicaragua/place/san-jorge/), where ferries depart for the island. The crossing is a distinct transport stage, requiring time to get to the dock, board and continue onward after disembarking.

When planning the journey, find out:

- which mainland port the ferry departs from and where it arrives;
- whether there is time to visit Ojo de Agua or go for a walk after the crossing;
- where the overnight stay is planned and how the return from the island works;
- what weather conditions or ferry schedule changes could affect the day.

Check the actual timetable before traveling. Wind and lake conditions can affect crossings, so a tight connection to an international flight immediately after the island section is unwise.

## How Ometepe appears on an Ada Tours itinerary

On the current [10-day “Best of Nicaragua” journey](/nicaragua/tour/best-of-nicaragua-10-days/), the island takes up parts of **days five and six**. Day five includes a transfer to San Jorge, the ferry to Ometepe and a visit to Ojo de Agua, followed by a night on the island. Day six brings the group back across the lake to San Jorge, then onward to [San Juan del Sur](/nicaragua/place/san-juan-del-sur/) on the Pacific Ocean.

The [ferry and Ojo de Agua excursion](/nicaragua/ometepe-island/ometepe-ojo-de-agua-ferry/) describes this portion separately. It is useful for finding out exactly what is included in the island day. **Climbing Concepción or Maderas is not part of the named 10-day itinerary.** That is the essential difference between a general island visit and a dedicated trekking program.

If you want more time on the volcanoes, the route and level of difficulty must be arranged separately; the availability of trekking on Ometepe does not itself establish that it is included in the tour price.

## When to visit and what to bring

In western Nicaragua, the broadly drier season runs from **November to April**, with rain more frequent from May to October. Around the lake, this affects comfort; on volcanic trails, it also affects traction, visibility and safety. The upper slopes can remain wet and cloud-covered even during relatively dry months.

For a general visit, pack light clothing, sun protection, closed-toe shoes for walking and a raincoat. Volcano ascents require more: grippy footwear, enough drinking water and fitness appropriate for the activity. Choose gear for the actual route rather than a generic description of the island.

## Frequently asked questions about Ometepe

### Is Ometepe in the sea or a lake?

It is in freshwater [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/). The Caribbean [Corn Islands](/nicaragua/place/corn-islands/) are a different destination in the country.

### Can we see both volcanoes in a single day?

Panoramic views of both massifs are available from various points on the island. Climbing both summits is an entirely different undertaking and should not be equated with a general tour.

### Is there an itinerary without difficult trekking?

Yes. You can choose lakeside scenery and a visit to [Ojo de Agua](/nicaragua/place/ojo-de-agua/). Exact stops depend on the selected program.

### How much of the journey does the ferry take up?

It is an essential stage for traveling between the mainland and the island in both directions. Departure, boarding and onward transfer times must be checked against current schedules and lake conditions.
